650e01bc5b4c7139da540eb70e787d154afb7103.summary: Project page for Havoc, a post-exploitation command and control (C2) framework with a Qt client, a Go teamserver and a C/ASM agent called Demon. It lists features and quick-start requirements. It is a software project page and marketing-style description, not a threat report on any actor, campaign or incident.

6584c7fa5f53f6fea9b65cfde0f82867b0bd742d.summary: Report on the US federal sentencing of Ukrainian Fedir Hladyr to 10 years in prison and $2.5 million restitution, for his alleged role as an administrator of the FIN7 cybercrime group. The report says FIN7 is alleged to have breached hundreds of US firms, used the front company Combi Security, and kept operating after arrests, including mailing malware-laced USB sticks in early 2020. Prosecutors estimated losses at $3 billion to $5.7 billion, against an earlier researcher estimate of $1 billion.

65fc9d406cde5d3458817e0c2da702ed7f7f4eaa.summary: Proofpoint report, dated March 14, 2016, on Carbanak group campaigns that targeted executives and staff at financial organizations in the Middle East, with later campaigns against U.S. and European targets. Delivery used phishing emails with exploit documents (CVE-2015-2545), macro documents and URLs. Payloads include Spy.Sekur, jRAT, Netwire, MorphineRAT and DarkComet. The report says some links to DarkComet and MorphineRAT are unproven. It also covers an older August 2015 Toshliph and CyberGate campaign.

hedges: Netwire may have been spread as part of the same campaign; no emails attempting Netwire infection were observed.
Connections between DarkComet/MorphineRAT and Carbanak are not proven definitively; the report offers several possible explanations.
Use of stolen or fraudulent signing certificates is not a strong indicator of Carbanak activity, since certificates may be available to other groups.
Targeting statistics come from logs and recipient data, with best-effort filtering of security researchers.
The ArabLab0 and TUBOR0 identifiers are hardcoded values, with ArabLab0 possibly used as a campaign identifier.
CVE-2014-6352 is described as likely exploited; one passage spells it CVE-204-6352.
The August 2015 Toshliph campaign is older than the rest of the document and is included for completeness.

658e0f6fd16ab07688366e37c17cfd418a0e4e59.summary: Cisco Talos reports TimbreStealer, a new obfuscated information stealer aimed at users in Mexico. It is spread through phishing emails with Mexican tax-invoice (CDFI) lures and compromised websites. Talos assesses with high confidence that the same threat actor earlier distributed the Mispadu banking trojan from September 2023. The report describes multi-stage decryption, anti-analysis checks, direct system calls, and browser and system data collection. Analysis of the final payload was still ongoing at publication.
